newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing share market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing share market report.

text.p: Dutch blue chips swept higher across the board in late trade to close nearly two percent up, buoyed by an early surge on Wall Street on the back of good macro-economic data and a sky-rocketing Bund future.
The AEX index closed up 13.58 points or 1.81 percent at 763.34 after spending the day in positive territory.

But dealers said volumes had stayed light throughout the session as players were disinclined to trade ahead of Wednesday's Queen's Day public holiday in the Netherlands and May Day closures on most other European markets a day later.
Tuesday's U.S. macro-economic figures were well-received.
First quarter labour costs rose by just 0.6 percent, well below the 0.9 percent consensus, while durable goods orders slumped by 3.0 percent in March.
The two reports would ease pressure on the U.S. Federal Reserve to hike interest rates in May to prevent the economy from overheating, economists said.
Guilder bonds surged on the news, taking their cue from a jump in the Bund future and lending added support to shares.
The AEX rise was further aided by Wall Street's opening surge, dealers said. "The figures were very, very nice," one said.
The only AEX component stock to end down was chemicals concern Akzo Nobel, which shed 1.50 to 251.00 guilders.

However the loss was optical, as the stock was trading ex a final dividend of six guilders and effectively shrugged off a broker downgrade in the wake of disappointing first-quarter earnings growth announced last Friday.
Fellow cyclical DSM added 4.20 guilders to 194.00 on first quarter profits slightly ahead of consensus.
The petrochemicals company said recovered margins and higher sales volumes had boosted net from ordinary operations to 223 million guilders from a year-earlier 216 million.
One of the day's biggest gainers in brisk trade was software house Baan which closed up six guilders at a new year-high of 102.10, off an intra-day peak of 104.50.

The stock was buoyed by news of a major Finnish order with an estimated worth of some $20 million, but later came off as Wall Street opened because its U.S. listed shares failed to perform in line with the gains in Amsterdam, dealers said.
Another major gainer was brewer Heineken, which added 10 guilders to 326.50 as bargain-hunters stepped in after the stock's recent losses.
Among the smaller caps, Schuttersveld plunged seven gulders to 86.50 after the industrial group reported first quarter net profits down five percent at 7.15 million guilders.

"The figures came in way below what everyone had been expecting," one dealer said. "They're maintaining their outlook of higher profits for the full year, but frankly I'm doubtful they will be able to make it."

Dealers said the overall market rise had been based on relatively low-volume trade, as many players stayed away ahead of a Dutch bank holiday on Wednesday and May Day closures in many other European markets on Thursday.
